text:
maria: Quick dump from a noisy nsys run on the dedicated pool node. TL;DR: large host->device memcpy bands line up with CPU scheduling gaps during KV prefetch, causing observed token latency regressions. attaching initial notes.

jon: can you paste the nsys command and a screenshot of the timeline? want to check stream ids and overlaps.

maria: command I used:```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,os,dmabuf --output=kv-prefetch-test nvproflike-run.sh
```

maria: screenshot attached (will upload to thread), but main observations:
- compute stream (s0) shows trt_infer_forward kernels interleaved with cudaMemcpyAsync on stream s2.
- memcpy bands are ~5-12ms each and repeated; during those bands CPU shows long preemptible gaps (green bars in nsight).
- kvcache_prefetch kernel appears to enqueue host copies that use stream s2, but copies sometimes block.

perf-bot: Profiling job kv-prefetch-test completed in 145s. {job_id: 2026-03-17-09}

jon: interesting — does the memcpy show as cuMemcpyHtoD vs cuMemcpyAsync pinned? nsight should show API call names on host timeline.

maria: yes, host timeline shows repeated calls to cuMemcpyHtoD_v2 and cudaMemcpyAsync (I think runtime picks async path but falls back to sync when pinned pool not available). stack traces show our prefetch thread calling cudaMemcpyAsync for small pages (~64KB chunks).

sam: small chunk copies + CPU preemption = lots of short DMA ops that serialize on the PCIe engine. If the prefetch thread is descheduled between enqueues and completions, device sees bursts of memcpy rather than steady overlap.

carol: did anything change in kernel selection/quantization branch last week? we had a change that increased prefetch granularity to 64KB -> 256KB as an experiment. that could alter how copies line up.

maria: good call — the A/B rollout did flip prefetch granularity to 256KB on canary. on the problematic node traces I see consistent ~256KB copy size. that suggests regression linked to that change.

jon: hypothesis: larger chunk size increases per-copy duration, so if the prefetch thread is on a CPU core that gets preempted, each preempted copy stalls a longer span, causing bigger memcpy bands that block compute overlap.

sam: we should also check pinned buffer pool exhaustion. If runtime fails to get pinned pages fast, cuda runtime may fallback to synchronous HtoD. nsight API trace will include return codes and pinned allocations.

maria: extracted a short host timeline snippet (aligned with device):```
Host timeline (ms):
0.0  | prefetch enqueue cudaMemcpyAsync 256KB -> stream s2
0.8  | prefetch enqueue cudaMemcpyAsync 256KB -> stream s2
1.6  | prefetch thread preempted (sched out) for 9.4ms
11.0 | prefetch resumes, issues cudaMemcpyAsync 256KB
11.7 | compute kernels on s0 stall waiting for KV pages
```

carol: that 9.4ms sched gap is huge. which kernel scheduling class is the prefetch thread running under? realtime? normal?

maria: normal niceness, pinned to utility pool. candidate issue: CPU contention from other processes (backup job) on the same host. I've correlated syscall activity spikes with the preemptions.

jon: actionable checklist: 
- reproduce on isolated node (no backup jobs)
- try reducing prefetch chunk size to 64KB to see if overlap improves
- instrument pinned pool allocation failures and record fallback to sync memcpy
- add nvtx markers around prefetch enqueue and host allocs to correlate in future traces

sam: also try switching the copy stream to a higher priority/compute-affine stream if hardware supports it (so DMA isn't queued behind low priority copies). but that's more intrusive.

maria: I ran quick A/B on isolated node: with 64KB I see memcpy bands shrink to ~2-3ms and compute overlap improves ~18% p50 token latency. With 256KB, p50 regresses ~12% — consistent with hypothesis.

perf-bot: Perf delta recorded: canary(256KB) vs baseline(64KB): p50 +12%, p95 +6% across 1k sampled requests.

carol: solid signal. short-term revert prefetch granularity to 64KB on canary. medium-term: make prefetcher adaptive based on observed CPU scheduling/host pinned pool health.

jon: let's also add an nsight run with CPU core pinning for the prefetch thread and mark the NVTX spans. share the capture id here.

maria: putting a patch for revert on canary now, will run isolated nsys with nvtx markers and upload timeline. attaching capture id: kv-nsys-197777-01.

sam: one more note: we should add a metric in console to show host memcpy bands per-minute for each node (count + avg duration) so we can alert on memcpy storms.

maria: agreed — filing a quick ticket for telemetry and the canary revert. thanks all. :thumbsup:

jon: 👍
